ITEM.PTXT: For a vehicle to drive, turn and stop, it is fundamental that the tires grip the road surface and perform their function as tires. However, during sudden braking or braking on slippery road surfaces such as snowy roads or puddles, the wheels may lock while the vehicle is still moving, causing slipping between the tires and the road surface. Therefore, ABS (Anti-lock Brake System) detects the wheel speed during such braking and controls the brake fluid pressure of all 4 wheels under computer control. This control prevents the tires from locking and ensures sufficient braking performance, thus maintaining steerability and vehicle stability.

In addition to conventional ABS functions, ABS with EBD appropriately controls the braking force of the front and rear wheels and of the left and right wheels regardless of load changes due to the vehicle being empty or loaded, ensuring excellent braking performance.

Front/rear brake force distribution control achieves an appropriate distribution of braking force to the front and rear wheels according to the vehicle driving conditions, with the aim of fully bringing out the "stopping" performance that is the basic function of the brakes.

As a result, the braking force of the rear wheels can be effectively used according to load changes due to loading conditions and deceleration, reducing the brake pedal effort particularly when loaded and ensuring excellent braking effectiveness.

Left/right brake force distribution control controls the braking force of the left and right wheels to ensure vehicle stability when braking during cornering, ensuring excellent braking effectiveness while maintaining vehicle stability during braking.
ABS is not a device that provides performance exceeding the capability of the tires; drive safely, paying sufficient attention to speed, following distance, etc.
Installing parts other than those specified, such as tires of other than the specified size, will adversely affect ABS control.
Motor noise may be heard due to the initial check immediately after the engine is started and the vehicle is driven for the first time; this is not a malfunction.
If the brake pedal is lightly depressed during the initial check, it may feel heavy; this is not a malfunction.
Under the following conditions, the braking distance when ABS operates may be longer than that of a vehicle without ABS.

ENTRY.PTXT: When driving on gravel roads or fresh snow
When driving over bumps such as road joints
When driving on rough roads such as uneven roads or cobblestones

ITEM.PTXT: Hydraulic pressure control of the 4 wheels is performed by operating the holding and pressure reduction solenoid valves, pump and reservoirs.
Brake assist control directs hydraulic pressure generated by the pump in the brake actuator to each wheel cylinder, generating hydraulic pressure higher than that of the master cylinder.

ENTRY.PTXT: Same as master cylinder hydraulic pressure

ITEM.PTXT: Hydraulic pressure generated by the pump in the brake actuator is directed to the wheel cylinders of each wheel, suppressing wheel slip caused by the driving force.

Hydraulic pressure generated by the pump in the brake actuator is directed to the wheel cylinders of each wheel, and the brake hydraulic pressure is controlled to suppress rear wheel skid or front wheel skid.
In rear wheel skid control, the front brake on the outer side of the turn is applied.

TABLE.TITLE: VSC Control Operation (Rear Wheel Skid Control)

ITEM.PTXT: For the front wheel not under control, the holding solenoid valve is turned ON (closed).
For the front wheel not under control, the pressure reduction solenoid valve is turned OFF (closed).
VSC control directs hydraulic pressure generated by the pump in the brake actuator to each wheel cylinder and controls the brake hydraulic pressure to suppress rear wheel skid or front wheel skid.
In front wheel skid control, the front wheel brakes and the rear wheel brake on the inner side of the turn are applied.

TABLE.TITLE: VSC Control Operation (Front Wheel Skid Control)

ITEM.PTXT: For wheels not under control, the holding solenoid valve is turned ON (closed).
For wheels not under control, the pressure reduction solenoid valve is turned OFF (closed).
For wheels not under control, the hydraulic pressure is held.

While the brakes are held, the M/C cut solenoid valves (No.1 and No.2) are closed so that a certain portion of the hydraulic pressure generated by the master cylinder remains in the calipers, performing hill-start assist control.
A semiconductor type speed sensor is mounted to the steering knuckle, and a magnetic rotor is mounted to the inner race of the hub bearing.
The magnetic rotor consists of rubber filled with magnetic powder, with N and S poles evenly arranged in the circumferential direction (48 poles each for S and N).
When the magnetic rotor rotates, changes in the magnetic field are produced; these are detected by the active sensor and output as vehicle speed pulses.
Compared with the commonly used passive sensor, detection is possible from a vehicle speed of approximately 0km/h.

On 2WD models, a semiconductor type speed sensor & magnetic rotor integrated with the bearing unit is provided in the axle hub, with the magnetic rotor mounted to the inner race of the bearing unit and the sensor mounted on the cap side.
On 4WD models, a semiconductor type speed sensor & magnetic rotor are provided, with the magnetic rotor mounted to the inner race of the bearing unit and the sensor mounted to the rear axle.
On both 2WD and 4WD models, the operating principle of wheel speed detection is basically the same as that of the front.

A steering sensor is provided in the combination switch. Detects the steering amount and direction and inputs them to the skid control computer.

The sensor section has 2 sets of magnetoresistive elements that detect the rotation of a magnet built into the detection gear, and detects steering rotation from the change in magnetic resistance as the detection gear rotates.

PARA.TITLE: Yaw Rate Sensor & Linear G Sensor

ITEM.PTXT: The semiconductor type yaw rate sensor and G sensor are integrated for compactness and mounted under the front passenger seat. When acceleration acts on the vehicle, the movable electrode in the G sensor moves, changing its distance from the fixed electrode; the capacitance between the electrodes is measured and converted into an electrical signal. By combining 2 G sensors, each mounted at an angle of 45 degrees relative to the longitudinal direction of the vehicle, deceleration can be detected in all horizontal directions, and together with the linear output characteristics, this allows precise control on various road surfaces.

The yaw rate sensor detects the angular velocity of the vehicle's rotation around its vertical axis (yaw rate) from the amount and direction of strain in a piezoelectric ceramic. Dedicated ICs are used for sensor body excitation and signal processing, reducing size and ensuring reliability.

Consists of master cylinder cut solenoid valves, holding solenoid valves, pressure reduction solenoid valves, a pump, reservoirs, etc., and regulates the brake hydraulic pressure to each wheel cylinder. In addition, the brake actuator and skid control computer are integrated to reduce size.

MECA.TITLE: Holding and Pressure Reduction Solenoid Valves

ITEM.PTXT: Two solenoid valves are operated by control signals from the skid control computer to switch the brake hydraulic circuit among 3 modes: pressure increase, holding and pressure reduction.
Linear solenoid valves are used as the master cylinder cut solenoid valves, smoothing hydraulic pressure changes during brake assist control.

By controlling the open and closed state of the valves, the hydraulic pressure generated by the pump is regulated, making it possible to generate control hydraulic pressure according to the operating condition.

The skid control computer processes the signals from each sensor and performs the brake control for ABS, TRC, VSC, hill-start assist control and brake assist. It also communicates with the engine control computer and outputs control signals.

The vehicle condition is determined from the information from the speed sensors, yaw rate sensor, linear G sensor and steering sensor, and when the vehicle is determined to have a tendency toward rear wheel skid or front wheel skid, brake hydraulic pressure control for each wheel, engine fuel cut control, etc. are performed according to the degree of that tendency.

When the drive wheels start to slip on a slippery road surface, etc., the wheel speed of the drive wheels greatly exceeds the estimated vehicle speed calculated from the speeds of the wheels that are not slipping. TRC control performs independent brake control of both wheels and engine control according to the amount of slip.

When the vehicle speed first reaches approximately 6km/h or more after the engine is started, each solenoid valve and the motor in the brake actuator are operated in sequence to perform an electrical check. During the initial check, operating sounds of the solenoid valves and motor may be heard in the engine room; this does not indicate a malfunction.
By connecting and operating a diagnostic tool, diagnostic trouble codes and computer data can be read.
